source_binding.text: **3.** 为作出球面镜所成的像，取什么光线为宜？

preoption_expected_domain: For a concave spherical mirror in the paraxial construction model, use rays from the same object point whose actual paths meet available reflecting surface.
A line directed through curvature center O is locally normal and reflects back along its incident path; this is reflection, not unchanged forward propagation through a lens.
A focus-directed incident line reflects approximately parallel to the principal axis; a parallel incident line reflects approximately through the concave principal focus.
At the pole P the principal axis is the local normal, so incident/reflected paths are symmetric about that axis if reflecting material exists at P.

Use two distinct usable paths sufficient to determine the image point, not duplicate drawings of one line or rays from unrelated object points. Use reflected-line intersections for a real image and backward extensions for a virtual image.
A central hole is not reflecting surface. A convenient path that would strike the hole must be replaced with one that actually strikes mirror material.
Common focusing and common image-point statements retain the small-angle/paraxial limitation. Local equal-angle reflection itself is not restricted to this approximation.
Convex-mirror focus statements, if introduced, must use backward extensions and virtual focus; do not claim actual rays pass behind the reflecting mirror.
source_supported_vs_clarification: Four construction rays and actual central-hole restriction are source-supported in d440. Distinct usable paths and appropriate extensions are independently recorded scientific clarifications, not captured bookRaw.
